sections.title: 1. About Pygame Zero
sections.body:
Pygame Zero is a beginner-friendly library that makes it easier to create games in Python. It is built on Pygame but hides complex details so you can focus on game logic.

Main advantages:

  • No need to write the main game loop
  • Simple syntax for graphics and sound
  • Great for learning programming

Simplest program example:

import pgzrun

WIDTH = 800
HEIGHT = 600

# Create an actor (sprite)
actor = Actor('alien')  # alien.png should be in the images/ folder
actor.pos = (400, 300)

def draw():
    screen.clear()
    actor.draw()

def on_mouse_move(pos):
    actor.pos = pos

pgzrun.go()

sections.title: 2. Objects
sections.body:
In Pygame Zero the main objects are sprites, also called actors (Actor). An actor is a sprite you control in code (move, rotate, and so on).

Creating an actor:

actor = Actor('image_name')

# You can set position and size right away
hero = Actor('hero', pos=(400, 300), size=(64, 64))

where 'image_name' is the image file name (without extension) in the images folder.

Tip: Images should be PNG or JPG and stored in the images folder.

sections.title: 3. Window
sections.body:
Game window size is set with WIDTH and HEIGHT at the start of your program. Set the window title with TITLE.

WIDTH = 800
HEIGHT = 600
TITLE = "My Game"

player = Actor('player')
player.pos = 100, 56

Coordinates start at the top-left corner (0, 0). Set an actor's position with pos or separately with x and y.

sections.title: 4. Redrawing
sections.body:
The draw() function is called automatically to redraw everything on screen.

def draw():
    screen.fill((135, 206, 250))  # sky
    player.draw()
    enemy.draw()
    screen.draw.text("Score: " + str(score), (10, 10), fontsize=22)

In PGZero Studio the screen is cleared automatically before each draw(). Use screen.fill(color) for a background or screen.clear() for a black screen. Use screen.draw.text() for text.

sections.title: 5. Sprites and properties
sections.body:
Actors have many useful properties:

  • pos — center position (x, y)
  • x, y — anchor point coordinates
  • size — size (width, height) in pixels
  • width, height — width and height separately
  • angle — rotation in degrees
  • scale — scale (1.0 = original size)
  • opacity — transparency (0.0–1.0)
  • image — current image name
  • anchor — anchor point, e.g. ('center', 'bottom')
  • flip_x, flip_y — horizontal/vertical flip
  • center, topleft, bottomright — corners and center
player = Actor('hero', pos=(400, 300), size=(80, 80))
player.angle = 45
player.scale = 1.5

# Change size later
player.size = (100, 100)
player.width = 90
player.height = 60

# Change image
player.image = 'hero_angry'

Useful movement methods:

player.move_forward(5)
player.move_towards(enemy, 3)
player.point_towards(enemy)
dist = player.distance_to(enemy)
size vs scale: size sets pixel dimensions. scale multiplies the image — beginners often find size easier to start with.

sections.title: 6. Moving sprites
sections.body:
Movement happens in update(), which runs before each redraw. You can accept a dt argument — seconds since the last frame:

SPEED = 200  # pixels per second

def update(dt):
    if keyboard.right:
        player.x += SPEED * dt
    if keyboard.left:
        player.x -= SPEED * dt
    if keyboard.up:
        player.y -= SPEED * dt
    if keyboard.down:
        player.y += SPEED * dt

If you don't need dt, write def update(): and move by a fixed number of pixels.

sections.title: 7. Keyboard
sections.body:
Pygame Zero gives access to keys through the keyboard object — good for checking if a key is held right now:

def update():
    if keyboard.space:
        fire_bullet()
    if keyboard.a:
        player.x -= 3
    if keyboard.d:
        player.x += 3

For one-time key presses use special functions and keys constants:

def on_key_down(key):
    if key == keys.SPACE:
        create_explosion()
    elif key == keys.ESCAPE:
        exit()

def on_key_up(key):
    if key == keys.SPACE:
        stop_charging()

Common constants: keys.SPACE, keys.ESCAPE, keys.UP, keys.DOWN, keys.LEFT, keys.RIGHT, keys.A … keys.Z.

sections.title: 8. Mouse events
sections.body:
Mouse events use special functions. Arguments: pos — (x, y) coordinates, button — mouse.LEFT, mouse.RIGHT, or mouse.MIDDLE:

def on_mouse_down(pos, button):
    if button == mouse.LEFT:
        print("Click at", pos)

def on_mouse_up(pos, button):
    if button == mouse.LEFT:
        print("Button released")

def on_mouse_move(pos):
    player.pos = pos

You can also check held buttons in update():

def update():
    if mouse.LEFT:
        player.angle += 2

On phones and tablets show on-screen buttons:

gamepad_show()   # show virtual gamepad
gamepad_hide()   # hide it

sections.title: 9. Sound and music
sections.body:
Short sounds use sounds; background music uses music.

# Sound effect
def on_key_down(key):
    if key == keys.SPACE:
        sounds.jump.play()
        sounds.jump.play(-1)  # loop
        sounds.jump.stop()

# Music
music.play('background_theme')       # loop
music.play_once('intro')             # once
music.set_volume(0.5)
music.pause()
music.unpause()
music.fadeout(2.0)
music.stop()

Files: short sounds in sounds, music in music. Formats: WAV, OGG, MP3.

sections.title: 10. Timer
sections.body:
Delayed code uses the clock module (or the same functions without clock.):

def spawn_enemy():
    enemies.append(Actor('enemy'))

# Every 3 seconds
clock.schedule_interval(spawn_enemy, 3.0)

# Once after 5 seconds
clock.schedule(game_over, 5.0)

# Don't duplicate if already scheduled
clock.schedule_unique(reminder, 10.0)

# Every frame (~60 times per second)
clock.each_tick(tick_animation)

def cancel_timer():
    clock.unschedule(spawn_enemy)

sections.title: 11. Drawing shapes
sections.body:
Besides sprites you can draw shapes and fills. Use Rect for rectangles:

def draw():
    screen.fill((135, 206, 250))  # background — RGB color
    ground = Rect(0, 500, WIDTH, 100)
    screen.draw.filled_rect(ground, (76, 175, 80))
    screen.draw.filled_circle((400, 300), 30, (255, 99, 71))
    screen.draw.line((0, 0), (WIDTH, HEIGHT), (255, 255, 255))
    screen.draw.rect(Rect(10, 10, 100, 50), (0, 0, 0))
    screen.draw.text("Hello!", (20, 20), fontsize=24, color="white")

Rect(x, y, width, height) creates a rectangle. screen.fill fills the whole screen; filled_rect and filled_circle draw individual shapes.

sections.title: 12. Collisions
sections.body:
Check collisions with actor methods and Rect:

def update():
    if hero.colliderect(coin):
        score += 1
        coin.x = random.randint(50, WIDTH - 50)

    if hero.collidepoint(mouse_pos):
        hero.opacity = 0.5

Main methods:

  • actor.colliderect(other) — overlaps another actor or Rect
  • actor.collidepoint((x, y)) — point inside actor bounds
  • actor.circle_collidepoint((x, y)) — point inside circle around center
  • Rect(...).collidepoint(x, y) — point inside rectangle

Actor inherits from Rect, so it also has left, right, top, bottom bounds.

sections.title: 13. Animation
sections.body:
There are two ways to animate a sprite.

1. Frame list — several images that switch automatically:

hero = Actor('hero_walk1')
hero.images = ['hero_walk1', 'hero_walk2', 'hero_walk3']
hero.fps = 8  # frames per second

def update():
    hero.animate()  # advances frames

2. Smooth motion — the animate() function:

animate(hero, pos=(500, 300), duration=1.0, tween='accel_decel')

# Available tween: linear, accelerate, decelerate,
# accel_decel, bounce_start, bounce_end, bounce_start_end

You can also change hero.image manually or call hero.next_image() to advance a frame.

sections.title: 14. FAQ — common code questions
sections.body:
Why won't the game start?
Check that the project has my_pgz.py, ends with pgzrun.go(), and Python indentation is consistent (4 spaces).

What are draw() and update()?
draw() draws the screen each frame.
update() moves characters and checks input.

How do I move the hero?
Change actor.x and actor.y in update(), or use keyboard.left, keyboard.right, and other keys.

How do I change sprite size?
Set size=(width, height) when creating the actor or later: actor.size = (64, 64). Or use actor.width and actor.height separately.

Why is the screen black or empty?
Add screen.fill(color) or screen.clear() at the start of draw(), then draw actors and shapes.

Where are images and sounds stored?
Images in images, sounds in sounds, music in music. Use file names without spaces, in Latin letters.

How do I draw my own hero?
Click Draw on the toolbar or in the image gallery, save the file, and use its name in Actor('file_name').

What if there is a code error?
Read the red message at the bottom, find the line number, and fix the typo. Common issues: missing :, wrong indentation, wrong image file name.
